#1802. John McGinn warns Tartan Army it might take 18 MONTHS for Scotland to click into gear under new boss Pocognoli

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:03 EST, 14 November 2026

Amid the clamour for a change at the helm following another poor showing at a major tournament, it was easy to lose sight of the reality of the situation.

Steve Clarke didn’t crash and burn in the US because a raft of world-class talents failed to turn up on the biggest stage. It happened primarily because a limited squad was unable to outperform two top-ten nations in Brazil and Morocco who could call upon infinitely superior footballers.

Sebastian Pocognoli has since arrived on the scene having earned a stellar reputation from his title success with Union Saint-Gilloise and his less feted spell at Monaco. But he has not come armed with a magic wand.

In opening the door to a string of fresh faces and advocating the more attacking approach which so many craved, the turbulence he’s experienced to date should only have been expected.

Limited by both the standard of players who are eligible for Scotland and the time he has to work with them, only the blissfully naïve would have seen his appointment as a quick fix.

While there were some positives to be taken from the game with North Macedonia – primarily the result – it’s likely the nation will have to endure more short-term pain for long-term gain.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets his players after a satisfactory evening at Hampden

This was always going to take time, perhaps, in the view of John McGinn, more than many may have imagined.

‘The manager’s got a great reputation, a good record at both places he’s been,’ said the Aston Villa captain. ‘The most important thing now in football is individuals don’t win you games. It’s unity, teamwork and everyone being on the same page.

‘You see how successful clubs and successful countries do it. And we want to be one of them.

‘It’s not going to happen overnight. There’s a lot to learn but we did create big chances against North Macedonia where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story.

‘But this isn’t something that gets fixed in March or even next September. It will start to build over the next 18 months.’

If that predicted time frame might raise an eyebrow or two, McGinn makes no apology for it. Call it managing expectations from the midfielder if you please. But without a degree of patience from the Tartan Army, he feels Pocognoli’s ideas won’t take root.

‘I understand it’s frustrating,’ he added. ‘It’s freezing and you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there.

McGinn sends his penalty home to give Scotland a deserved lead against North Macedonia

‘They’re entitled to their opinion, but there’s got to be a mixture of patience.

‘The supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys and just let the young ones flourish and try and settle into the team.’

Give credit where it’s due. With Clarke accused of causing stagnation by selecting the same old faces, Pocognoli has capped five players for the first time while recalling the likes of Oli McBurnie.

The sages in the stands can’t have it both ways. If the squad was going to evolve, it was never going to be a smooth ride.

‘I think the young players are starting to show more now,’ McGinn stressed. ‘Luke Graham on Friday night, I thought he was brilliant. It’s not easy playing in the middle of a back three. He’s been waiting for his chance and the manager’s shown that if you deserve your chance you’re going to get put in there.

‘We’ve got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to the pitch.’

Even in victory, McGinn doesn’t dispute that there is significant scope for improvement. He’s convinced, however, that this will all come good in the end.

McGinn insists it's vital the entire Scotland squad buy into the methods of manager Pocognoli

‘We need to play slightly better,’ he said. ‘We know that, but we’re going through a period which I’ve been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to.

‘And it’s about sticking at it. We’re keen to play a style of football that’s not easy but is going to get bums off seats. It’s important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn’t believe in it, that’s when it all starts to fall apart.’

Friday was another memorable night on a personal level for McGinn. Having broken the tension with the opener only to see North Macedonia level, he held his nerve to put Scotland back from the penalty spot.

The brace put him on 24 international goals, now within six of Denis Law and Kenny Dalglish. But all of that is for another day.

‘It feels a bit strange, but at the minute that’s gone to the back burner,’ he stressed. ‘I had a wee chat with Scott (McTominay) about the penalties. I was designated penalty taker but, to be fair, he’s not missed one I don’t think in his career.

‘So, we had a wee chat and I think we both said the most important thing was just no matter who hit it, hit the back of the net.’

McGinn is eyeing three points against Switzerland in St Gallen to close the campaign on a high

Tomorrow, the equation is clear. To finish second in the Nations League group and secure a place in pot two for the Euro draw, Scotland must beat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t beat North Macedonia.

Even if everything clicks for Pocognoli’s side, it will be the tallest of orders.

‘Difficult,’ said McGinn. ‘I know they drew on Friday night (with Slovenia) but they’ve got a couple of players back that they were missing last time.

‘It is a tough one but we want to be competing against these teams away from home. It’s not going to be perfect for a while, but we’ll stick at it.’

#1801. Quill confident Dallas are ‘well-oiled machine’ for playoffs

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Eric Quill believes FC Dallas are a "well-oiled machine" going into the MLS Cup Playoffs and is excited to see what they can do in the first match of Round One against the Portland Timbers.

Dallas finished second in the Western Conference to ensure they had home advantage in the best-of-three series, having finished the regular season with just one loss in their last six games (W3 D2).

They recorded their best finish since 2016 when they topped the West, and they have qualified for the playoffs in back-to-back seasons, though they were knocked out in Round One last year.

Quill is confident Dallas can improve on that result, though, claiming the drop in temperatures will only play into his team's strength on the press.

"We are a well-oiled machine right now, as far as across the board, just guys, how bought in they are and how much they're up for this," Quill told MLSSoccer.com.

"And our team speed, our pressing ability, the change of weather going into the high 60s, low 70s, is only going to help our game model, because we want to press and be really proactive, front-footed.

"We're going to be on people from minute 1 to 95."

The stage is set Our Round One playoff schedule is locked in. https://t.co/bv1xI7bAdu

— X – FC Dallas (@FCDallas) November 8, 2026

Portland, meanwhile, just snuck into the automatic playoff spots due to a strong finish to the regular season.

They went unbeaten in their last five games, winning each of the last four (D1), including a 2-0 win over Austin FC on Decision Day, which meant they pipped the Seattle Sounders to seventh.

"When we look at the progress, there have been some improvements, but you need to be consistent in that," head coach Marti Cifuentes said.

"We have to learn to be ourselves, whatever the game scenario. If we start well, then we need to keep on our philosophy.

"But obviously there is an opposition as well. There is always an opponent that prepares well for the game, and that's why the game is so beautiful, because sometimes you just need to cope with the reality of the game.

"I would say we need to at our best in our key identity and principles of the game."

Joaquin Valiente got the scoring started for Dallas in their win over the Rapids on Decision Day, netting just his third goal of the season.

He has been an effective playmaker, though, with nobody on the team bettering his 13 assists, while he also topped the charts for crosses (115) and chances created (48).

Jimer Fory has helped keep the Timbers ticking throughout the season, with no Portland player registering more touches (2,016), interceptions (63) or possessions won (161).

Only Finn Surman (1,570) attempted more passes than the Colombian (1,437), but Fory was a solid presence at the back with more successful tackles (32/54) than anyone else.

Dialed in the details https://t.co/QpLaIlYwN0

— Portland Timbers (@TimbersFC) November 18, 2026

Dallas have never won a postseason clash with Portland in 90 minutes (D2 L2). They lost in the first round in both 2015 and 2018, but advanced in 2020 after winning on penalties.

Dallas are unbeaten in their last six regular-season matches against Portland (W3 D3), with all three victories coming on home soil. In fact, they are unbeaten in their last seven at home against the Timbers.

Portland's last win against Dallas came back in June 2023 (1-0 at home), and while they have not won at Toyota Stadium since November 2018 (2-1), that victory was in the postseason.

#1800. Man Utd transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino puts prolific 19-goal Spurs target on January 'wishlist'

By Lewis Blain | 19 Nov 2026 07:21

Manchester United are preparing to strengthen their attack in the January transfer window, with new boss Mauricio Pochettino already keen to add more firepower.

The Argentine is understood to have put four main centre-forward targets on his winter 'wishlist', including a prolific striker also attracting interest from former club and top-flight rivals Tottenham Hotspur.

Benfica talisman Vangelis Pavlidis has emerged as a particularly exciting possibility after an outstanding start to the season in Portugal.

The Red Devils are ready to spend significantly to back Pochettino in January, with Benfica striker Pavlidis among the names under consideration, according to reports.

Spurs and Barcelona have also been linked with the Greece international, who is said to be open to a move to the Premier League in 2027.

One source revealed: "Pochettino is eager to make sure United have more of a goal threat. He's already been discussing names, and Vangelis Pavlidis is someone who fits the bill."

Pavlidis is not the only striker on United's radar, with Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen also admired by Pochettino. However, a deal for the Nigerian is considered less realistic due to his substantial transfer fee and wage demands.

Former Brentford forward Ivan Toney is another option, while Borussia Dortmund's Serhou Guirassy is being monitored as a potential rotation option, too.

Pavlidis has scored 19 goals in 19 appearances across all competitions this season, while also providing four assists. His remarkable return means he has found the net once every 72 minutes on average.

The 27-year-old's immense goalscoring numbers make him an attractive proposition for United, particularly with Benjamin Sesko having struggled with injuries.

His current form suggests he could provide an immediate improvement to Pochettino's attacking options, offering a reliable source of goals during the second half of the campaign.

Importantly, Pavlidis' age does not necessarily have to come at the expense of Sesko's long-term development, with the Slovenian still viewed as part of United's future once fully fit.

Osimhen may be the more ambitious acquisition, but Pavlidis appears to offer a potentially more attainable solution without sacrificing significant attacking quality.

If United are serious about challenging at the top end of the Premier League, adding a striker with 19 goals already this season could be a major step forward.

#1798. 'Dad, we are not walking out of the match. It's my first time in Old Trafford!' - An afternoon with my 10-year-old inside the Theatre of Screams for Carrick's last stand

Published: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026

‘Mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers. Will you join us?’ he asks earnestly, handing me a leaflet that announces: ‘Enough is Enough! Empty Old Trafford! Leave the stadium in the 21st minute. 21 years of failed ownership. Glazers OUT! Ineos OUT!’

More than 70,000 spectators leaving their seat and walking out of the stadium in the 21st minute have been quite the statement, especially live on Sky Sports.

But as admirable as Saeed TV’s aim is (I discover later he is some sort of youtuber), it’s hard to see gain any traction.

‘Dad, we are not walking out of the match. It’s my first time in Old Trafford,’ I am told as we continue to meander up Matt Busby Way, a declaration from my 10-year-old that causes a fair bit of mirth among the crowd.

Mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers. Will you join us?’

‘What’s wrong with the owners anyway?’ Dan enquires innocently, which leads to a bind.

How deep down the rabbit-hole should I go with my ten-year-old on his first visit to the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s probably not the time or place to try and explain leveraged buyouts and how much debt the Glazers have saddled the club with, £1.2 billion at the last count while taking millions out of it in dividends. Do I need to go further back and talk about Rock of Gibraltar’s unexpected success on the track and the concept of stud fees?

‘They are not putting enough money into the team and taking loads of money out of the club,’ is all I offer.

‘When Manchester City need a midfielder, they can buy Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez while United have to make do with someone who was sitting on Chelsea’s bench.’

He doesn’t look convinced that’s much of a reason to walk out of a football but as the cathedral of consumerism that is the Manchester United megastore has appeared, he forgets about United’s disastrous ownership model – for now, at least.

During his doomed attempt to coax Jurgen Klopp to Old Trafford around 2014, Ed Woodward apparently told him that United was the sporting version of Disneyland.

And to be sardined inside the megastore in the couple of hours before kick-off, you have to accept that the much-maligned former CEO may have been right about one thing.

Think Arnott’s a couple of days before Christmas, just with a lot more people. You even need to pass through airport-like security before even entering and spend your dosh.

One of the common refrains among United supporters is why are the Glazers holding onto the club when they don’t even seem to care.

Thirty seconds inside the megastore on match-day and you realise why the Americans are so keen to hold onto the asset they’re bleeding dry – and they probably care a great deal.

Dan gets obligatory photo at statue of United's holy trinity, a moment he will look back on

Even with the team languishing in the relegation zone, having won a single league game all season, people are keen to spend, spend, spend.

I see people wandering around with five or six different shirts, from different eras (I did succumb and bought Dan the black shirt from 95-96 season, because it reminds me of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and better times!)

You can get a photo with a replica of a Premier League trophy. That’s just £10. Or Lego sets of Old Trafford or the Munich clock.

That will just set you back £25.  For many in this shop, it seems allowing the club to empty their wallet is as much a part of the day as the actual football.

There are other parts of the ritual, which remain and have yet to be infected by the poisonous atmosphere around the club – and remind the three dads bringing their kids to Old Trafford for the first time of better days.

Such as curry chips and battered sausage from Lou Macari’s chipper. And the customary photo in front of the statue of the holy trinity of Best, Law and Charlton.

The megastore was the one place that seemed immune to the toxicity in the air. Once outside again and all that could be heard was the moans and groans, mainly because Shea Lacey wasn’t starting.

Coming here since the 1990s, we have seen the skyline of Manchester transformed as it became a sleek, modern city. It seems the one place that hasn’t changed is Old Trafford. It has remained the same.

Stuck in time. It looked sleek and modern in 1999, but now there is a tired, decrepit feel to the stadium – and not just because of the leaking roof. It could do with a lick or two of paint.

Stuck in time. It looked sleek and modern in 1999, but now there is a tired, decrepit feel to the stadium

No wonder Big Sir Jim is determined to plough ahead with his plans to make a crudely-designed circus tent ‘the Wembley of the North.’ Not that there is anyone inside Old Trafford of the same mind.

Senne Lammens has just trotted onto the field with Tom Heaton and Karl Darlow to do their pre-match warm-up when the chants start, telling Jim Ratcliffe he can stick his new stadium up his posterior.

It is a weird atmosphere, with all the chanting against the owners – both Glazers and Ineos – and nothing being sung in support of the players.

As my friend points out it must be so difficult for the team to show the best of themselves when things are this toxic in the stadium.

Dan has been to the Jodi Stand enough times on a Friday night to know there is plenty of choice and crude language at football matches, but still I nearly felt at covering his ears at some of the stuff being sung in Old Trafford last Sunday, especially that directed at CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

We had hoped that things might have been different when the game kicked off, but within a minute, Aston Villa had scored.

And three minutes later, they had scored again when Lammens fumbled Alysson’s shot into Nicolas Jackson’s path. Maybe walking out in the 21st minute wasn’t such a bad idea.

The crowd’s ire had gone from the owners to the players now, with a sustained chant of ‘You are not fit to wear the shirt.’ United did rally and by half-time, it was 2-2. But the mood was still dismal as we queued for a quick beer.

The 1958 Group had asked fans not to buy booze, another protest against the owners. But it seemed nobody was paying much attention to that.

One of the issues at United is that there seem to be too many splintered fan groups – there is also ClaimBackUnited and Fan Coalition ’58 – as well as Saeed TV, who seemed to be on his own solo run.

We didn’t feel bad about ignoring the booze ban, as everyone was doing it. And within a couple of minutes of the second-half, we saw the reason why. You need to fortify yourself to watch Diogo Dalot try to defend.

For much of the second-half, it seemed like Michael Carrick’s brief tenure was going to peter out in a forgettable defeat, as Villa seemed to manage the game perfectly.

Dan and his friends were growing frustrated, pointing out the players weren’t doing what their coaches tell them to do on a weekly basis, leading me to conclude that maybe my son’s under-11 side are better-coached than United.

The last on-pitch act of Carrick's tenure

And then there was the chaotic and crazy final few minutes in stoppage-time. And a draw that came out of nowhere and was celebrated like a victory.

That was the thing. Even though the mood inside the stadium was toxic for most of the game, even though the team were two down inside four minutes and the season has been a disaster, everyone still came away from Old Trafford, happy and with a smile on their face.

Only football can do that. More than that, perhaps only Manchester United – despite everything – can do that.

#1797. Chelsea transfer news: Blues learn new asking price for in-demand forward amid Man City interest

By Lewis Blain | 19 Nov 2026 07:39

Chelsea are facing growing competition for Club Brugge forward Nicolo Tresoldi, with Premier League rivals Manchester City among the clubs monitoring his situation.

The 23-year-old has attracted considerable attention after an impressive goalscoring campaign in Belgium, with several European sides now considering a move.

However, the asking price for the Germany-born striker has risen amid increasing interest, potentially complicating the Blues' pursuit.

Tresoldi has scored 14 goals in all competitions for Club Brugge this season, including five in the Champions League, with his hat-trick against Inter Milan a particular highlight.

North London duo Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with the forward, while Serie A giants Juventus and AC Milan are closely monitoring his availability.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Milan are currently considered the leading contenders, with Tresoldi's support for the Rossoneri potentially helping their pursuit.

However, Chelsea and City remain in the picture, although their chances of securing his signature could be complicated by Club Brugge's increasing demands.

Tresoldi was initially valued at more than €50m (£42m), but it is now believed that the Belgian outfit wants €60m (£50m) as they look to capitalise on the growing interest.

Milan are keen on a January move, with the player's preference for a switch to San Siro potentially giving them an advantage. Ultimately, though, their ability to meet Brugge's asking price could determine whether a deal is possible.

Although Tresoldi's performances make him an attractive target, Chelsea's chances of landing the forward appear rather complicated.

His preference for AC Milan is an obvious obstacle, particularly with the Italian club already keen to explore a January transfer.

There is also the question of where he would fit into Xabi Alonso's plans, with Joao Pedro currently Chelsea's first-choice centre-forward. City face a similar dilemma, given Erling Haaland's established position in their attack.

For Tresoldi, regular football should be an important factor in deciding his next move, particularly at this stage of his development.

Chelsea may therefore be better served exploring alternative forward options rather than committing significant resources to a player who could favour a move elsewhere and face competition for minutes at Stamford Bridge.

#1796. Pochettino determined to ‘change things’ at Man Utd

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino believes it is a "mistake" to solely focus on Manchester United's current predicament, and vows to "change things" at the club.

Pochettino began his tenure as United boss on Wednesday, leaving his position as United States head coach after signing off with a win in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals against Haiti.

He is tasked with improving United's current position, with the team sitting 18th in the Premier League table after the first 10 games.

The Red Devils have won just one of their first 10 matches in the league (D5 L4), while they are winless in eight Premier League matches for just the second time, also doing so in April/May 2025.

By the time United kick off against Liverpool in Pochettino's first game in charge, they will have been in the drop zone for 15 consecutive days – their longest run of days in the top-flight drop zone since September/October 1986 (28 days).

But Pochettino does not want to focus on the negatives, instead choosing to be optimistic about what United could do.

"It's a mistake to see the situation," Pochettino told United's social channels. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"It's about to start to act and to change things, and to try to affect, in a good way, all the areas, to try to really believe that we can recover that feeling about to win.

"The most important thing is for us to start to work hard to recover that feeling. That feeling is about being winners, to win games, to perform. But that is not only to talk about winning."

The importance of Sunday's fixture isn't lost on Mauricio

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 19, 2026

Reports suggest Pochettino will have a say in whatever business United do in the January transfer window, but he has over a month until he can add reinforcements to his squad.

United have 10 games to play before the end of the calendar year, and the Argentinian is determined to get the best out of his current crop of players.

"The best request that we can have, the players that we have, and we need to love the players that we have," Pochettino added.

"We need to support the players; we need to provide all the tools for their performance.

"It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the possibility to translate all their talent on the field."

Pochettino will be the first-ever United manager to see his first league game come against rivals, Liverpool.

Just one of the Red Devils' last nine managers (incl. caretakers) has lost his first Premier League game of a spell in charge of the club (W4 D4), with Erik ten Hag losing 1-2 to Brighton in August 2022.

Though Liverpool are the favourites to win – with the Opta supercomputer giving them a 57.3% chance of victory on Sunday – Pochettino has his eyes on three points.

"We are going to go there, to Anfield, with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United," he said.

"We need to make sure that we are brave, and we are protagonists, and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool."

#1795. “He will be in charge” – Di Marzio clarifies positions of Krösche and Ibrahimovic

Gianluca Di Marzio has confirmed Markus Krösche’s imminent arrival, and that he will be given the reins to take AC Milan forward.

It is not exactly a well-kept secret that Milan have been pursuing Krösche. He was the main target in the summer to come in and lead the management, but Eintracht Frankfurt blocked his exit. Now he has stepped down from his role there, a move to Italy has been in the headlines again.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Several sources have reported that the Rossoneri have an agreement in place with the German director to come in and be the new Head of Football. In other words, he will be the main man on the sporting side, and will offer some support to head coach Ruben Amorim.

What kind of relationship will the former Eintracht executive have with Zlatan Ibrahimovic? Gianluca Di Marzio spoke about it live on Sky, and his comments were relayed by MilanNews.

“Ibrahimovic has never been in charge of AC Milan, not when he left, nor when Tare left, nor during the interregnum. Cardinale is in charge now because he is Amorim’s true point of reference,” he began.

“The coach is there, and there will be the new Head of Football, Marcus Krosche. He will arrive from Eintracht, and now all that’s waiting for this agreement to be formally finalised. He will be in charge, and Ibrahimovic will stay on as he is now, that is, as a consultant to RedBird and Cardinale.

“But as you’ve seen, since the start of the season he’s been to Milanello once and to San Siro once or twice. He’s not the one in charge of AC Milan operations right now.”

#1794. NEC vs PSV Eindhoven - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 08:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:42

The 2026-27 Eredivisie season resumes with NEC welcoming PSV Eindhoven to Stadion de Goffert on Saturday evening, as both teams kick off matchday 13.

Both sides recorded impressive victories in their final outings before the November hiatus and will be aiming to build on that momentum.

With Feyenoord and Ajax dropping points against Heerenveen and FC Twente earlier in the day, PSV travelled to the Kooi Stadium to face Cambuur with the opportunity to move top of the Eredivisie table - a chance they seized emphatically with a 5-2 triumph.

That was a much-needed response from Peter Bosz’s men, who had suffered a 2-1 defeat to Club Brugge in the Champions League just four days earlier.

Playing before their title rivals gives De Rood-witten the chance to open up a four-point gap at the summit with a victory this weekend. However, away matches at NEC have been challenging recently, with the last four yielding just one win and 12 goals conceded.

PSV’s trip to Nijmegen is further complicated by a daunting assignment against Real Madrid next Tuesday, leaving Bosz with a delicate balancing act, especially after an international break in which several players were involved.

With a league-high six goals scored in the opening 15 minutes this season, Saturday’s visitors have an opportunity to exploit a notable weakness in NEC, who have conceded first in six of their last eight matches and in eight of the last 10 meetings between the sides.

After a difficult start to the season, NEC appear to be getting back on track, as a 3-2 victory over FC Utrecht on November 8 secured back-to-back wins for the first time since August and made three victories from their last five outings (D1, L1).

While confidence appears to be returning, Dick Schreuder’s side have yet to solve their defensive issues, conceding in 19 consecutive matches across all competitions; their last shutout came in the season opener against Olympiacos.

Having failed to keep a clean sheet in 20 consecutive meetings with PSV, the Eniesee know they will need to deliver in attack to stand any chance of success and have shown they can, scoring at least three goals in five of the last six encounters against this weekend’s opponents.

Saturday’s hosts also face a looming European assignment, giving Schreuder additional selection considerations as he seeks a third consecutive win over his opposite number in 2026, following two victories in March just 11 days apart.

For all of NEC’s recent renaissance, they are one of two Eredivisie teams - alongside Willem II - yet to win a league home match this season, so there is bound to be some level of apprehension among the supporters.

Emre Mor (groin) and Bram Nuytinck (ankle) have both been sidelined since September and remain unavailable for NEC.

Perr Schuurs is a doubt for this weekend after missing the win over Utrecht, while Dennis Geiger is still regaining full fitness.

Bryan Linssen has scored or assisted in each of his side’s last four meetings with PSV, and the veteran forward will be aiming to make an impact once again.

Ex-NEC player Sami Ouaissa will not feature against his former club due to a muscle problem that has hampered his debut campaign in Eindhoven.

Long-term absentees Adamo Nagalo, Jerdy Schouten and Alassane Plea are all still a long way from returning to action.

Meanwhile, Paul Wanner is set to make his comeback after the November international break, but Saturday’s clash is expected to come too soon for the Austrian.

Crettaz; Bras, Kaplan, Fonville; Kers, Nejasmic, Lebreton, Bakker; Chery, Tadic; Linssen

Kovar; Kostic, Obispo, Geertruida, Dest; Mauro Jr, Mijnans, Sano; Van Bommel, Til, Bajraktarevic

The last four meetings between PSV and NEC have produced a combined 24 goals, and all the evidence points to another entertaining encounter on Saturday.

PSV have shown vulnerability away from home at times, while NEC have yet to hit their stride in front of their own fans. Nevertheless, we expect PSV’s attacking threat to edge a high-scoring contest.

#1793. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

September 12: Liverpool vs Fulham (Premier League)September 15: Liverpool vs Tottenham (League Cup)September 20: Bournemouth vs Liverpool (Premier League)October 11: Liverpool vs Manchester City (Premier League)October 14: LASK vs Liverpool (Champions League)

"It's difficult to ask for more." 👏Andoni Iraola reflects on Liverpool's winning start to their Champions League campaign.🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vDH7bob0V8

Tonight: Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1 (home)October 14: LASK (away)October 20: Villarreal (home)November 4: Fenerbahce (away)November 25: Club Brugge (away)December 9: Porto (home)January 19: Inter Milan (away)January 27: Lens (home)

Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

So far, four of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season have played on this opening matchday and all four have won:

Tuesday:Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3Porto 0 Manchester City 2

Tonight:Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Napoli 0 Arsenal 1

The final English club in action will be Manchester United tomorrow night, who host Azerbaijan newbies Sabah.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Andoni Iraola celebrates his first Champions League win as Liverpool boss! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/9XDUOprvS7

Barcelona 5 Feyenoord 1 Stuttgart 3 Viking 1 Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1 Napoli 0 Arsenal 1 PSG 6 Slovan Bratislava 1 Sporting 3 Galatasaray 1

Possession: Liverpool 45%-55% Atletico MadridShots: 14-9Shots on target: 5-4Corners: 7-5Touches in opposition box: 31-18

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

"We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Barcelona 5 Feyenoord 1 FTStuttgart 3 Viking 1 FTLiverpool 1 Atletico Madrid 1 HTNapoli 0 Arsenal 0 HTPSG 3 Slovan Bratislava 0 HTSporting 1 Galatasaray 1 HT

Possession: Liverpool 50%-50% Atletico MadridShots: 6-6Shots on target: 3-3Corners: 3-1Touches in opposition box: 17-3

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

Atletico Madrid: Oblak; Llorente, Pubill, Romero, Hancko; Simeone, Barrios, Koke, Baena; Alvarez, Lee.Substitutes: Musso, Vargaz, Mendoza, Cardoso, Lookman, David, Grimaldo, Hjulmand, Le Normand, Dominguez, Martinez, Castillo.

"This is big boys' football." 💪Steve McManaman says Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz need to step up for Liverpool on the biggest stage 👀🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/umLHH8lPU4

"I actually think Liverpool need him." 👀Steven Gerrard and Steve McManaman discuss the importance of Alexis Mac Allister to Liverpool.🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M12Asjv79V

Let's get to work, Reds 😤 pic.twitter.com/HLo8079Wme

"It's a big night, a big game." 🔥Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola looks ahead to tonight's Champions League opener and provides the latest on Cody Gakpo's fitness 👀🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qi9rj7xQuV

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

Atletico Madrid: Oblak; Llorente, Pubill, Romero, Hancko; Simeone, Barrios, Koke, Baena; Alvarez, Lee.Substitutes: Musso, Vargaz, Mendoza, Cardoso, Lookman, David, Grimaldo, Hjulmand, Le Normand, Dominguez, Martinez, Castillo.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Tonight: Atletico Madrid (home)October 14: LASK (away)October 20: Villarreal (home)November 4: Fenerbahce (away)November 25: Club Brugge (away)December 9: Porto (home)January 19: Inter Milan (away)January 27: Lens (home)

Barcelona 2 Feyenoord 0 (46’)Stuttgart 3 Viking 1 (47’)Liverpool vs Atlético Madrid 8pmNapoli vs Arsenal 8pmPSG vs Slovan Bratislava 8pmSporting vs Galatasaray 8pm

Ready for #UCL action 👊🔴 pic.twitter.com/XyOupLwsRe

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1791. ​Women’s Super League predictions: Arsenal, Chelsea and Man City backed as big favourites on MD11

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The 2026-27 Women's Super League season is already 10 games in, and both ends of the table are taking shape.

Charlton Athletic remain without a point to their name at the foot of the standings, but above them, Birmingham City, Crystal Palace, Brighton and Liverpool are all clustered within five points of each other.

At the summit, Chelsea sit one point above reigning champions Manchester City, while London City Lionesses are flying high in third place.

Arsenal have a lot of ground to make up, but they are made the biggest favourites for MD11 when they host West Ham this weekend.

Chelsea face Liverpool, and Man City take on Tottenham in some intriguing matchups. Here, we use Opta insights and the supercomputer to look ahead to the WSL action.

It's heating up at the top of the #BarclaysWSL table https://t.co/weclTxN0Gy

— Barclays Women's Super League (@BarclaysWSL) November 16, 2026

Chelsea have won 17 games against Liverpool in the WSL (D4 L5), their joint-most victories over any one side in the competition (also 17 wins v Everton).

And Opta's model is forecasting another Chelsea victory at St Helens Stadium, with the Blues handed a whopping 70.4% chance of victory.

That makes them the most favoured away team on MD11 by some distance, with Liverpool's 13.1% win probability coming in higher than only two other sides.

Liverpool have won only five of their 26 WSL meetings with Chelsea (D4 L17), though each of the most recent four of those have come at home, most recently in May 2024 (4-3).

Chelsea have won each of their last six WSL away games, only once before having a longer winning run on the road in the competition, eight straight wins between August 2015 and September 2016.

The Blues' expected goal difference of +25.3 is more than twice that of any other side in the WSL this term, with London City next on +11.7. Sonia Bompastor's team have both attempted the most shots (228) and faced the fewest (72), taking more than three for every shot allowed.

It feels unfair to label London City as a surprise package this season, given the investment into their squad this past summer. Can a team with a Ballon d'Or holder in their ranks really be considered a surprise package?

Putellas has created 18 chances, provided one assist and scored three goals already in the WSL, and her form has been integral to London City sitting in third place ahead of hosting Crystal Palace.

London City are the clear favourites, with a win likelihood of 67.2% to Palace's 14.8%. There is an 18% chance of a draw.

Palace have, however, won their last two away league games against London City without conceding (1-0 in 2022-23, 2-0 in 2023-24), though they have already lost away to the Lionesses in this season's Players Cup (2-4).

But Palace are winless in their last 14 away games in the WSL (D5 L9), since a 2-0 victory at Leicester City in October 2024. Having drawn each of their first three away matches this season, the Eagles have lost both of their last two.

London City have won six of their last seven WSL home games (L1), scoring at least twice in every victory.

Mary Earps at full stretch #BarclaysWSL | @LC_Lionesses https://t.co/sFSOanUDhk

— Barclays Women's Super League (@BarclaysWSL) November 15, 2026

Manchester United are fourth, eight points behind leaders Chelsea, and they are the favourites to take three points against next-to-bottom Birmingham.

The Red Devils have a 60.1% win probability, while Birmingham have a 19.2% chance.

After a difficult start under new boss Eva Olid, United are unbeaten in their last eight WSL games (W5 D3), having lost their opening two this season.

The Red Devils have conceded just four goals during this run, compared with seven in those first two matches, and have kept a clean sheet in each of their last three.

Ella Toone has scored (three goals) or assisted (two assists) in all four of United's WSL games against Birmingham. No fixture has been played more often in the competition with the same player registering a goal involvement in every meeting.

Spurs are unbeaten in three league games, and that form has taken them to fifth in the standings.

However, they are not given much of a chance against Manchester City, who have a 74% win probability. Spurs come out on top in just 10.8% of the supercomputer's simulations.

City have won 12 of their 13 WSL games against Tottenham, with the exception being a 2-1 home defeat in September 2021.

And Spurs have lost six of their last seven away matches against City in all competitions (W1), averaging over four goals conceded per defeat (26 in six).

City have won each of their last 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026; only Chelsea have ever won more home matches in a calendar year, winning 11 in both 2022 and 2023.

Double digits in Europe Bunny Shaw makes more history after her goal against BK Häcken! https://t.co/2nKTU104bK

— Manchester City Women (@ManCityWomen) November 19, 2026

Charlton Athletic are only the third side to lose their opening 10 games of a WSL season, after Doncaster Rovers Belles in 2016 and Yeovil Town in 2017-18. Those teams did not collect their first points until their 16th and 13th matches, respectively.

And while the supercomputer expects it to be close between Charlton and Aston Villa, the Villans are anticipated to take the points (42.6% to Charlton's 32%). There is a 25.4% probability of a draw.

Villa have taken four points from their last two league away games (W1 D1), twice as many as across their previous five (D2 L3); the Villans have lost just one of their five matches on the road this season (W1 D3).

Charlton have conceded nine set-piece goals in the WSL this season, at least three more than any other side and accounting for 30% of their goals against (9/30). Six have come from corners, also the most in the division, while the Addicks are yet to score via one themselves.

Everton sit eighth on the back of three straight draws, but those all came against teams above them in the standings (Spurs, Chelsea and Man Utd).

They now host Brighton. Everton have never drawn four consecutive games in the competition, with their only other run of three coming in their first three WSL fixtures in April 2011.

The Toffees are the favourites, with a 43.5% win probability, but at 26.8% this is the game that is most likely to be a draw, with Brighton's chances ranked at 29.7%.

Everton have kept a clean sheet in three of their last five WSL home games, as often as across their 23 home matches prior; the Toffees themselves could go goalless in back-to-back home matches in the league for the first time since November 2023, however.

Between the 2018-19 and 2023-24 seasons, the head-to-head record between Everton and Brighton in the WSL was perfectly balanced with four wins each (D4) – since then, however, the Seagulls have won all four of their top-flight meetings with the Toffees.

Everton surpassed 250 @BarclaysWSL matches on Saturday – the Toffees being only the third team to reach the milestone. If you know your history. https://t.co/i5VfwXUf6n

— Everton Women (@EvertonWomen) November 16, 2026

The most likely winners on MD11 are Arsenal (76.1%), as they host West Ham, who are handed just a 9.7% win probability.

With just three wins from their opening 10 matches (D5 L2), Arsenal have recorded their fewest victories at this stage of a season. Their 14 points are also their joint-lowest tally after 10 games, alongside 2014.

West Ham have won three of their last five WSL games (L2), having won just one of their opening five this season (L4); the Hammers' four victories are already three more than they had recorded at the same stage last term (one).

Arsenal are the first team to draw each of their opening five home games of a WSL season, with the last four all finishing 1-1. The Gunners are nevertheless unbeaten in their last 24 home matches in the competition (W16 D8), since a defeat to Chelsea in October 2024.

But they will now be looking to bounce back from a disappointing 2-0 home loss to Lyon in the Women's Champions League on Thursday.

The Gunners have won all eight of their WSL home games against West Ham by an aggregate score of 27-8, always scoring at least twice in those matches.

#1790. Dida discusses Endrick rumours, Torriani’s growth and ‘great coach’ Amorim

Nelson Dida believes that Ruben Amorim is showing he is a ‘great’ coach, and he gave his take on the Endrick to AC Milan rumours.

If anyone knows about the pressure of playing for Milan, it is Dida. Having been at the club from 2000 to 2010, he made over 300 official appearances for the Rossoneri and was part of an era that brought in eight major trophies under Carlo Ancelotti.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He is widely regarded as one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation and was decisive in the 2003 Champions League final penalty shootout against Juventus. He also returned briefly as a goalkeeping coach, working for a year with Maignan.

Dida spoke to reporters who were present at the Galbiati Trophy and he answered a few questions regarding his former team, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

“Amorim is proving to be a great coach. He took over Milan and is having a fantastic season. I think the attention is right because at Milan you can never make mistakes, but he has the ability to keep the team together to do well in the league.”

If Maignan is hurt, would you come back and put the gloves on?

“We already have a goalkeeper at AC Milan: Lorenzo Torriani, a guy who’s doing well. I like him. Last year, too, he did well when he had opportunities. I think he’s a focused guy, if he gets more opportunities, he can continue to grow.”

“Milan are slowly growing. They’re doing well in the league, I think we can still do more, while in Europe we’re still missing something.”

“Endrick is a great player for me. When I see him play, he looks a bit like Romario, who is a bit small, but when he’s in the penalty area, he’s decisive. When he’s had the opportunity to play, he’s also scored goals.

“I think he can really do well for Real Madrid and the national team, but I don’t know if he’s available to join Milan. I hope a Brazilian returns to play in the Italian league soon and wears the Milan shirt.”
